identity.description:
Resume a stopped eval run, and plan one D4b baseline

Make the eval resumable, and plan one D4b baseline at the end.

A baseline at two repeats does not fit in one five-hour plan window, the eval and the CI reviewer use the same plan login, and a stopped eval run lost every result. This PR fixes the last point and changes the D4b plan.

## What changes

- Each finished repeat writes `<out>/<case>/<repeat>/result.json`: the `RepeatMetrics`, the case name and head, the repeat number, the tool version and the options that change a result (tier, judge model, extras, raw judge). A temp file and a rename write it, so a kill leaves no half file.
- `pr-review eval --resume` reads those files before the first model call. A repeat with a good result is reused: no clone and no model call. A failed, missing or unreadable result, or one for another case head, clears that repeat's output and runs it again. A result of another tool version or with other options stops the command with exit 2, so one report never mixes two configurations. Reused results go through the report, the gate and `--write-baseline` like fresh ones. Stderr says how many repeats were reused.
- README: a "Resume a run" section and the `--resume` flag.
- TICKETS.md, D4b: no revision moves the pin or writes a baseline. One final baseline PR moves the pin one time and writes the baseline at two repeats, with `--resume`.
- Version 0.7.0 for the new flag.

## Verification

- New tests in `test/eval-cli.test.ts`: a run that fails on the third case, then `--resume` on the same `--out`, makes model calls only for that case, and the aggregate equals that of one uninterrupted run; a reused repeat makes no call; a failed result runs again; another tool version gives exit 2; without `--resume` every repeat runs.
- `npm test` (1297 tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `scripts/check-version-bump.sh` pass.

triage.summary: Adds a --resume option to `pr-review eval`. Each finished repeat now writes an atomic result.json with its metrics, case head, tool version and result-affecting options. With --resume, non-failed matching results are reused with no model call. A tool version or option mismatch exits 2, and a stale or failed repeat has its output cleared and is rerun. The change includes tests, docs, ticket text and a version bump to 0.7.0.

findings.claim: The description says each finished repeat writes result.json, but a write failure only prints a warning and the run continues, so a later --resume runs that repeat again.
findings.suggested_fix: In the README, say that a failed write of result.json gives a warning and that --resume then runs the repeat again.
findings.explanation: The description and README do not say that a failed write of result.json is only a warning.

findings.claim: The version and option checks run before the failed, case and head checks, so a failed or stale result that would be rerun anyway still stops the whole resume with exit 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip failed results and results with another head or case before the version and option checks.
findings.explanation: A result that will not be reused cannot mix configurations, so it should not block the run.

findings.claim: readResult does not check that `repeat` is a number or that it matches the repeat slot, so a malformed file with both repeats missing, or a file with the wrong repeat, is still reused.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `typeof value.repeat === "number"`. In reusableResults, also check `found.repeat === repeat`.
findings.explanation: If both fields are undefined, the check passes. A file with a repeat number other than its directory then feeds metrics for the wrong repeat into the report.

findings.claim: No test covers the case where a result is not reused because its case head sha differs.
findings.evidence: if (found.metrics.failed || found.head !== c.head || found.case !== c.name) continue;
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that edits head in result.json, then runs with --resume and asserts that the repeat runs again (a triage call is made).
findings.explanation: If the head check breaks, a stale result from an older case revision would be reused in the baseline without warning, and no test would fail.

findings.claim: No test checks that a rerun repeat's old output is cleared, so the repeat dir ends up with exactly one record.
findings.evidence: await rm(join(out, c.name, String(repeat)), { recursive: true, force: true });
findings.suggested_fix: In the resume test, assert that recordsUnder(join(out,'c-planted','1')) has length 1 after the resume.
findings.explanation: If the rm breaks, the repeat dir would hold the old failed record next to the new one, and no test would fail.

findings.claim: No test covers the path where result.json cannot be written and the eval only warns.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that makes the result path unwritable, then asserts exit 0 and the warning on stderr.
findings.explanation: No test checks that a failed write lets the run continue with a warning instead of aborting.

first.rationale: The code matches the claim. readResult never checks that `repeat` is a number, so two undefined values pass the comparison. reusableResults never compares `found.repeat` with the loop's `repeat`. This only happens with a hand-edited or moved file, because writeResult always writes a matching repeat, so it is an edge case and the fix is cheap.
